name: John Vincent
bio: John Vincent is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 7th Congressional District. His campaign says he served 20 years in the U.S. Navy and later built a small business. He says he will not accept corporate PAC donations.

platform.point: End tariffs, protect Social Security, raise wages and make home ownership more attainable.
Restore small-business programs, give farmers stable trade policy and expand career-focused training.
Keep rural hospitals open and preserve health care tax credits.
Keep commitments made to veterans, teachers and first responders.
Support term limits, a ban on congressional stock trading, limits on dark money and a balanced budget.

economy.evidence: Wants to end tariffs while also calling for higher wages and budget discipline.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and health care tax credits and keep rural hospitals open.

notes: Hometown and details of his business are not stated on the campaign site.

name: Marty Jackley
bio: Marty Jackley has been South Dakota Attorney General since 2023, a post he also held from 2009 to 2019. He was U.S. Attorney for the District of South Dakota from 2006 to 2009 and ran unsuccessfully in the 2018 Republican primary for governor. He is from Sturgis, South Dakota, and owns a farm and ranch.

platform.point: Give police, sheriffs and prosecutors the tools and support to keep violent criminals off the streets.
Secure the border and finish construction of the border wall.
Push for fair markets, honest trade and less federal red tape for farmers and ranchers.
Defend gun rights, which he calls non-negotiable.
Back President Trump's agenda including tax cuts.

economy.evidence: Backs tax cuts and less Washington regulation for agriculture.

liberty.evidence: Guns: calls gun rights non-negotiable and cites an NRA A+ rating; the cited page does not address abortion, drugs or LGBTQ issues.

security.evidence: Pledges to give police and prosecutors more tools to pursue violent criminals.

immigration.evidence: Pledges to secure the border and finish the wall.

notes: Liberty was lowered from 50 to 30 after an unverified claim about his marijuana prosecutions was removed, leaving only gun-rights evidence. The Commons portrait dates from 2006.

name: Nikki Gronli
current_role: Small-business owner; former South Dakota state director of USDA Rural Development
bio: Nikki Gronli led USDA Rural Development in South Dakota from 2022 to 2025, overseeing rural housing, broadband and infrastructure investments. She has nearly three decades of experience in marketing and communications and now owns a small business. She lives near Dell Rapids and has served on boards including the Minnehaha County Housing and Redevelopment Commission.

platform.point: Support rural small businesses, workforce training and infrastructure, and lower housing, childcare and energy costs.
Protect Medicare and Medicaid, restore marketplace tax credits and address rural EMS and nursing home gaps.
Oppose farm consolidation, remove tariffs on farm inputs, and back mandatory meat labeling and year-round E15 sales.
Fully fund IDEA, protect Title I funding, support teacher pay and make sure rural schools get adequate resources.
Increase Medicaid funding for home-based care and protect voting accommodations.

economy.evidence: Wants tariffs on farm inputs removed but also opposes farm consolidation and billionaire economic dominance and backs legal action against meatpackers.

welfare.evidence: Wants to protect Medicare and Medicaid, restore marketplace tax credits and expand Medicaid home-care funding.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: says government should stay out of medical decisions and supports bodily autonomy.

education.evidence: Calls for full IDEA funding, higher teacher pay and investment in rural public schools.

notes: A trade item sourced to a South Dakota Searchlight article was removed because the article could not be opened to confirm it.

name: Diana Harshbarger
bio: Diana Harshbarger has represented Tennessee's 1st Congressional District since 2021 and serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee. A pharmacist trained at Mercer University, she has run a pharmacy business since 1987. She was born in Kingsport, Tennessee.

platform.point: Lists defending life as a priority and supports anti-abortion legislation.
Supports a border wall and stronger immigration enforcement.
Opposes new gun restrictions such as background checks on private transfers.
Prioritizes rural broadband expansion and rural health care access.
Opposes tax increases and voted against the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act.

economy.evidence: Opposes raising taxes, including on the wealthy.

welfare.evidence: Opposes the Affordable Care Act and opposed expanding coverage of anti-obesity drugs.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: anti-abortion; guns: voted against background checks for private transfers.

security.evidence: Favors stricter punishment as a crime deterrent and keeping existing police accountability rules.

immigration.evidence: Supports a border wall and opposes a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

foreign.evidence: Voted against the 2024 $60 billion Ukraine military aid package.

notes: No campaign website was found this pass.

name: Kristi Burke
bio: Kristi Burke is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 1st Congressional District. She is a muralist and YouTuber who describes herself as a community member rather than a career politician. Her campaign focuses on grassroots organizing across the district.

platform.point: Create a universal single-payer system through Medicare for All.
Shift the tax burden from working families to corporations and the wealthy and close special-interest loopholes.
Fully fund K-12 public schools, oppose vouchers and make community college tuition-free.
Oppose mass deportations and family separation in favor of a lawful, humane system.
Regulate tech companies to protect personal data and prevent manipulation.
Put diplomacy ahead of military intervention and avoid wars of choice.

economy.evidence: Wants to shift taxes onto corporations and the wealthy.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: protect access to abortion and birth control; LGBTQ: equal protection for LGBTQ people.

security.evidence: Calls for police accountability within clear constitutional limits.

immigration.evidence: Opposes mass deportations and family separation.

foreign.evidence: Rejects wars of choice and prioritizes diplomacy.

energy.evidence: Pledges to hold corporate polluters accountable and protect natural resources.

tech.evidence: Wants regulation of tech companies to protect personal data.

education.evidence: Calls for full public school funding and opposes vouchers.

faith.evidence: Supports separation of church and state with a neutral government.

name: Tim Burchett
bio: Tim Burchett has represented Tennessee's 2nd Congressional District since 2019. He previously served as Knox County Mayor from 2010 to 2018 and in the Tennessee House and Senate from 1995 to 2010. He is a Knoxville native and a University of Tennessee graduate.

platform.point: Finish the border wall, end catch-and-release and deport people who entered illegally.
Reverse federal overspending and treat taxpayer dollars with care.
Abolish the U.S. Department of Education and return decisions to states and localities.
End government cover-ups and overclassification.
Protect unborn life and oppose federal funding for abortion.

economy.evidence: Opposes raising taxes on the wealthy and voted against debt-limit deals without spending restraint.

welfare.evidence: Wants to repeal the Affordable Care Act in favor of free-market policies.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: opposes abortion and its federal funding; guns: lifetime NRA member who opposes background-check requirements.

immigration.evidence: Supports the wall and deporting those who entered illegally while welcoming legal immigration.

foreign.evidence: Initially opposed U.S. intervention in Iran and has been skeptical of foreign entanglements.

energy.evidence: Wants offshore drilling restrictions lifted and opposes greenhouse gas regulation.

tech.evidence: Opposes net neutrality and voted against internet regulation.

education.evidence: Advocates abolishing the Department of Education in favor of state and local control.

notes: Foreign-policy record is mixed: he supports Israel aid and later endorsed the 2025 Iran strikes, and sources disagree on his Iraq AUMF vote. No campaign website was found this pass.

name: Michaela Barnett
bio: Michaela Barnett is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 2nd Congressional District. She is a civil engineer and small-business owner who recently spent a year working in Congress. She is based in the Knoxville area and grew up doing farm work.

platform.point: Pass laws that put workers and families ahead of the wealthy.
Make care affordable and accessible, judged by patient outcomes rather than profits.
Regulate AI and large data centers and protect residents' privacy.
Bring federal infrastructure investment to East Tennessee.
Reduce corruption and corporate influence in politics.
Expand affordable housing.

economy.evidence: Favors legislation that benefits workers and families over the wealthy.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports reproductive freedom; LGBTQ: defends LGBTQ rights; guns: supports responsible gun ownership.

immigration.evidence: Calls for a commonsense, dignified immigration system.

tech.evidence: Plans to regulate AI and large data centers.

notes: Her issues page gives few specifics, so the energy and education scores rest on brief statements.
